title: A Bullied Coward Stopped The Deadliest Fighter Alive With One Punch . . . (Full Story)

segments.say: A school coward who once begged for his life just *punched* the deadliest man alive, and the whole room froze.
That man is Goomoonryong, the Nine Arts Dragon, and seconds earlier he *butchered* a whole building full of fighters.
The kid in front of him can barely stand, covered in blood, but he still *refuses* to run away.
To see how it got here, go back to a very ordinary *school*, where nothing special happens to anybody.
Shi-woon Lee is a quiet high school kid, and Changho's gang uses him as a *punching* bag every single day.
Every hallway is a trap, and he comes home with a new *bruise* more often than he comes home with homework.
Changho's gang demands sixty thousand won from him, and he has no idea how he is going to *pay* it.
Her name is Sae-hee, she is the girl he likes, and he is far too scared to ever *talk* to her.
Today she sees his battered face in the hallway, and she just stares in *shock*.
He is so ashamed that he snaps at her to stay out of it, and rips his arm *away*.
Then a new substitute teacher walks in wearing a flowery *shirt*, and asks a student where the school office is.
His name is Han Chun-woo, and he looks like a washed-up beach *bum* who got lost on the way to a vacation.
He spots Shi-woon's bruises and calls him a *coward* who cannot even hit back, which is a hell of a first impression.
Rude, but not exactly *wrong*.
Han took a quiet job at a quiet school, hiding from his past, and he picked the worst possible *school*.
In class, Shi-woon keeps his head down and prays that nobody, especially the teacher, will notice *him*.
Then Changho barks at the new teacher to stop screwing *around* and start the lesson, like he owns the place.
Han just grins and tells the whole class to open their *books*, and somehow Changho shuts up.
That night, outside a Muay Thai gym, a pack of thugs *surrounds* the strange new teacher.
Han takes one thug's insult as a *compliment*, then kicks the whole room across the floor like he is speedrunning a video game.
Shi-woon watches from the doorway and realizes this clown in the flowery shirt is no ordinary *teacher*.
Shi-woon starts to wonder who his teacher really is, and Han wants to keep it a *secret*.
The next day, Changho's boys drag Shi-woon aside, and a bully blows smoke in his face and tells him to shut up and *take* it.
They throw him around until he is on the floor, and all he can do is *apologize*.
Nobody helps, everybody *watches*, and the girl he likes sees every second of it.
That is the moment Shi-woon decides the world would be better off without *him*.
Up on the school roof, he starts to think the only way out of this life is *down*.
He climbs up to the ledge, and the second he slips, he screams *save* me.
And who hears him? The weird substitute, who yells at him to hurry up and *jump*, if he is going to.
Han yanks him up, makes him promise never to jump again, and then the rusty railing *snaps*.
They both fall off the roof and crash straight onto the vice principal's brand new *car*.
Shi-woon gets up with barely a scratch, and has no idea how he is *alive*.
Even Han looks confused about it.
The vice principal's car is totaled, and he grills the whole school, asking if anybody *saw* anything.
But the bullying does not stop, and Changho now wants Sae-hee *delivered* to his gang behind the school gym.
Terrified, Shi-woon runs back to the new teacher and *begs* him for help, because he has nobody else.
Han says he is only a temporary teacher, and he will be gone in two *months*, so it is not his problem.
He tells Shi-woon to solve his own problems, and just walks *away*, hands in his pockets.
Shi-woon screams that he is a coward, and that is exactly *why* he is asking for help.
So he fights Changho's boys alone, loses again, and crawls back to Han on his *knees*.
He begs Han to teach him martial arts, so he can finally stand up to those *punks*.
That took more guts than any punch.
Han finally says yes, but only if Shi-woon is willing to risk his *life*, because a fighter's body is not worth much without it.
Then he drives the boy to a bridge at night, and tells him to *jump*.
Shi-woon jumps, and for one long second, he is *sure* he is dead.
Han hauls him out, ruins his fancy shoes, and drags him to the *hospital*, complaining the whole way.
Imagine nearly dying just to sign up for *karate* class.
Han makes him promise he will never jump off the school roof again, which is honestly *fair*.
From then on, Shi-woon is Han's student, and the training is pure *torture*, from the first push-up to the last.
Laps around the track, then more laps, and if he faints, Han says *more* laps.
Shi-woon throws up, collapses, and cries, but he is back on that field the next *morning*, which already makes him tougher than Changho.
Two weeks in, he can run one lap without throwing up, which for him is basically a *miracle*.
Han teaches him to breathe slowly and deeply, because he says a strong *body* is only the start.
He calls it ki, the energy inside every martial artist, and says it matters more than any *muscle*.
Meanwhile the new health teacher, Shiho, is obsessed with Han, and he runs from her like she is a *tax* collector.
Shiho keeps flirting, Han keeps dodging, and the vice principal keeps almost having a *heart* attack.
Her wild Lamborghini ride leaves Shi-woon dizzy, like he just stepped off a *roller* coaster.
He is still weak, but for the first time in his life, he *shows* up every single day.
A Lamborghini suddenly shows up in the faculty parking lot, and the vice principal cannot stop *staring* at it.
Then a gang boss named Song shows up, hunting a martial artist called the Nine Arts *Dragon*, and he does not look friendly.
Han lights a cigarette, says he does not want trouble, and bares a dragon *tattoo*.
That mark belongs to the Dragon, a legend of the Murim, the hidden world where martial arts clans still *rule*.
Song's men laugh, and that is the last *mistake* they ever make.
One soul-crushing punch, and the boss's iron hand turns into a bloody *mess*.
Shi-woon sees it all, and finally understands why his teacher was never afraid of *Changho*.
Never insult a man holding a cigarette.
Han hates attention, but trouble finds him anyway, like a bad *sequel* nobody asked for.
Back at school, Changho's gang corners Shi-woon again, expecting the usual *routine*, like he is a vending machine for punches.
This time he does not crawl, and the whole hallway hears the *crack* of a fist.
Then men in expensive suits roll up to the school in a black *Maybach*, and every student stops to stare.
Their young master is hunting the Nine Arts Dragon, and he is *not* polite about it.
In this world, martial arts clans hide behind ordinary jobs, and their fights decide who runs the *shadows*.
Behind closed doors, the Nine Clans argue over who will find the Dragon *first*, and nobody wants to share the credit.
Soon Shi-woon is ambushed on a dark highway by a pack of bikers, and he has no *chance*.
Then Han appears and screams, do you know whose *disciple* you are messing with?
The bikers hear the name Goomoonryong, and the color drains from their *faces*.
Han turns the whole gang into scrap metal, and it is a full Hulk *smash*.
That is what a teacher is for.
Then Sae-hee is snatched off the street by a van, and Shi-woon screams her name as he *chases* it.
He tracks the thugs down alone, and walks in with his *fists* up, shaking but standing.
The training kicks in, and for once he is the one *swinging*.
He saves her, and Sae-hee asks softly if he was really *scared*, and he admits he was.
Main-character energy, finally unlocked.
Rumors travel fast, and soon every gangster in the city is whispering about the Nine Arts *Dragon*.
Shi-woon only wants to learn, and tells Han he will *protect* his friends one day.
Han shrugs, but he keeps teaching him, and Shi-woon *grins* like an idiot.
Years ago, Han lost control of his rage, and the Murim elders branded him a *monster*.
Now the Alliance wants him, and they decide Shi-woon is the perfect *bait* to lure him out.
Men in suits search the school, and Shi-woon is the first thing they *check*.
The old masters agree to trap Goomoonryong in a business *tower*, and they are very proud of the plan.
Ten old men against one teacher.
Shi-woon hears about it, and runs to *warn* him, because he refuses to be a burden anymore.
He races toward the tower, even though the elders are tracking his *phone*, which is a rookie mistake.
Then he grabs the phone and tells the driver to stop the car, because he will lure the trackers *away* himself.
Han storms in with Shiho at his side, and she says she is fine because she is with the *invincible* Goomoonryong.
At the tower, the chief sets off a fire alarm, and every coward runs for the *stairs*.
Han climbs up anyway, alone, with a smile on his *face*, like a boss walking into the final level.
The chief greets him, welcome Goomoonryong, you are a little *late*.
It was a trap from the start, and poison gas starts *flooding* the room.
Weakened and poisoned, Han stares at the chief, and something inside him *breaks*.
The poison and the old rage push him into a terrifying *form*, and the room goes quiet.
He tears through the Alliance's best, and every blow shakes the *tower*, like Saitama on a bad day.
Bodies fly, glass shatters, and the old men finally look *scared*.
That is not a human anymore.
Then a bleeding Shi-woon walks in and asks, Sunsengnim, can you *hear* me?
Han does not know him anymore, and he nearly punches his own student to *death*.
But Shi-woon keeps getting back up, and says, if it weren't for you, I would be dead, and this is not the Sunsengnim I *believe* in.
He tells him he used to be a coward who even thought of killing himself, and that Han is the one who *saved* him.
And then he throws one *punch*.
That punch stops the Nine Arts Dragon *cold*, and every fighter in the room asks if that kid really just did that.
Then Han strikes his own student straight *through*, and the whole room thinks he just killed him.
Han goes after the chief, but Kang-sung, the Alliance's top fighter, steps in and says the old man is already as good as *dead*.
Han just laughs and says that kid was only a *toy*, never his disciple, while Shi-woon lies there in his own blood.
Kang-sung admits Han killed his master, says he does not *blame* him, and the two monsters clash anyway.
The Alliance escapes in a *helicopter*, and Kang-sung promises there will always be another chance.
Shi-woon wakes up in a hospital, and learns Han destroyed his ki center, so he can never use martial arts *again*.
Han probably did it to *save* him, because a boy with no martial arts is no disciple the Murim needs to hunt.
Han, Shiho and even Sosul vanish like they never existed, and Shi-woon keeps calling, but nobody *answers*.
All Han leaves behind is a video on a new phone, teaching him one more ki *technique*.
Meanwhile Han is out there wrecking drug lords around the world, and the Murim's pride is in *pieces*.
The Sunwoo clan elders still want Shi-woon as their heir, because a boy who cannot fight makes an obedient *puppet*.
Men in suits show up at his school and bow to him, and Shi-woon tells them they have the wrong *person*.
They do not budge, they came for Goomoonryong's disciple, the new head of the Sunwoo *clan*.
The punching bag who begged for his life on that roof stopped the Nine Arts Dragon with one punch, and that is the *end*.
